passage: The Nakamura group investigated turnover of c-Myc, a regulatory protein that is rapidly degraded in proliferating cells. To measure stability without confounding new synthesis, cells were treated with cycloheximide, an inhibitor of translation elongation, and harvested at the times shown. Lysates were resolved by SDS-PAGE, transferred to a membrane, and probed with an antibody against c-Myc; band intensities were quantified and normalized to a loading control. Degradation of c-Myc was assumed to follow first-order kinetics. The researchers hoped to compare half-lives under normal and stressed conditions and to learn whether proteasome inhibition would stabilize the protein. Results from unstressed cells are shown; each value is the mean of three biological replicates, with errors below 5% of the mean. Equal total protein was loaded in every lane, as confirmed by the loading control. All procedures followed the laboratory's standard operating protocols, and raw data were archived before analysis.

questions.stem: What fraction of c-Myc remains 120 minutes after cycloheximide treatment?
questions.explanation: At 120 min, two half-lives have elapsed (100 → 50 → 25%).
questions.trap: Counting one half-life (50%) or three (12.5%) instead of the two half-lives that have elapsed; with a 60-minute half-life, 75% would be the amount lost.

questions.stem: Why is cycloheximide used in this experiment?

options.A: It accelerates proteasomal degradation of all proteins
options.B: It labels the protein for detection by antibody
options.C: It blocks new synthesis so that the loss of existing protein can be followed
options.D: It increases transcription of the gene

questions.explanation: Without blocking translation, newly synthesized protein would obscure the decay of the pre-existing pool.
questions.trap: Thinking cycloheximide accelerates degradation or labels the protein, rather than blocking translation so the decline reflects decay of the existing pool only.

questions.stem: If the decay continues to be first-order, what percentage of c-Myc remains after 240 minutes?
questions.trap: Miscounting the half-lives (3 gives 12.5%, 5 gives 3.125%) or reporting the 93.75% lost instead of the 6.25% remaining.

questions.stem: Which statement about first-order decay is INCORRECT?

options.A: The rate of decay is proportional to the amount remaining
options.B: The half-life equals ln 2 divided by the rate constant
options.C: The half-life increases as the starting amount of protein increases
options.D: The half-life is independent of starting concentration

questions.explanation: In first-order kinetics, t½ = ln 2/k and does not depend on starting concentration.
questions.trap: Believing a larger starting amount means a longer half-life; in first-order decay the half-life (ln 2 / k) is independent of the starting amount.

questions.stem: c-Myc turnover is typically controlled by which system?

options.A: Ubiquitination and degradation by the proteasome
options.C: Glycosylation in the Golgi apparatus that prevents degradation
options.D: Phosphorylation by glycolytic kinases that leads to secretion

questions.explanation: Polyubiquitin chains (K48-linked) mark proteins for proteasomal degradation; proteasome inhibitors such as MG132 stabilize short-lived regulatory proteins.
questions.trap: Choosing a glycosylation, phosphorylation or lysosomal option because it sounds like regulation, when short-lived regulators are tagged with ubiquitin for proteasomal degradation.
